payload.rebuttal: argued: The task's own Out of Scope section already names this exact failure mode, citing the same two facts the critic cites: set_task_package never clears merged_head_sha, and a CHANGES_REQUESTED row sits in scheduler.REQUEUE_STATES. The spec accepts it for a stated reason: cli._resolve_queue (the one shared path saffron queue and saffron batch both use to decide what to run) calls reconcile before it calls build_queue, and build_queue is the only place REQUEUE_STATES drives a resume. I verified this ordering still holds at head. So for any row that crashes after this fix is deployed, the next scan's reconcile call completes it to MERGED on the already-true old head before build_queue ever sees it as resumable in that same call, and if reconcile itself raises mid-scan, build_queue does not run at all that scan. saffron cell's attended path never consults REQUEUE_STATES either, since that resume decision belongs only to the scheduler. The scenario the critic describes therefore requires a row that already crashed and was already resumed and repackaged with a new pr_url under the old, pre-fix reconcile, before this change was deployed. That is precisely the migration-period exception the spec names and accepts, not a defect this diff introduces.
